author: assistant (claude-opus-5), M2 P2.22
constraints: n is between 1 and 1000. The graph holds no cycles and no repeated edges.
edge_cases: A node with no incoming path has an empty list. A node is not its own ancestor.
input_semantics: Two parameters. The first, n, is the number of nodes labelled 0 to n-1. The second, edges, is a list of directed node pairs.
load_bearing: An ancestor is any node with a directed path of one or more edges to the node, and each node's list is sorted ascending and free of repeats.
output_semantics: A list of n lists. The entry at each position holds that node's ancestors in ascending order.
required_operation: For every node of a directed acyclic graph, find all nodes from which it can be reached, and report them in ascending order.
source_basis: The question title and the boilerplate method name, both from this project's own bank. The bank stores NO problem description — its content field holds a placeholder and a generic example — so the behaviour described here comes from the assistant's own knowledge of the canonical task. No sentence is copied from any external problem statement.
title: All Ancestors of a Node in a Directed Acyclic Graph
